notes:
Jolof Empire, additions batch af-03-x; Cliopatria has no row (its Mali shape covered Senegal to 1415). Pages: Jolof Empire, Battle of Danki.

Disagreements: Sine and Saloum leave in 1520 (Jolof page) or at Danki 1549 (Danki page, which also names Wuli and Niani); Futa Toro 1513 (text) versus 1512/1514; the Jolof infobox lists Mali, Takrur and Sine as predecessors ambiguously. Dates not on the pages: Cayor/Baol absorption (before 1390, bridged 1360), Sine/Saloum absorption (late 14th century at the earliest, bridged 1390), Biram Njeme Eler's conquest (c. 1450s, bridged 1455). The Bambuk conquest is disputed (Boulègue). Mali dossier already holds a jolof-empire vassal_end in 1360.

Needs dossiers: jolof-kingdom (rump 1549-1890; the page does not date the end), cayor (Kayor, from 1549), waalo, baol, sine, saloum, futa-toro (Denianke, written in this batch if budget allows). The regions here are admin1 proxies for the Wolof/Serer states.

Revised 2026-10-19 after the review (verdict fail): (a) Sine and Saloum are no longer Jolof land: /ledger/3 and /ledger/7 became vassal_start 1390 (c1) and vassal_end 1520 (c3) cp sine, and Fatick and Kaolack are out of the 1390-1519 shapes (the keyframes 1361/1390 and 1513/1520 merged). Saloum has no event: the Kingdom of Saloum page says it 'was never a part of the empire' and dates the kingdom to c. 1494, while the Jolof and Danki pages list it among the tributaries; the disagreement is not settled. The jolof successors list loses sine and saloum (tributaries, not land handed over). (b) The 1455 gain names 'Namandirou (Takrur region)' as counterpart, since the takrur dossier ends in 1285; its land and that of the 1513 loss is the middle Senegal valley strip (river 40 km from Dagana to Bakel minus the Saint-Louis region), not the gazetteer 'Futa Toro' box. (c) Disagreement with the reviewer on /ledger/5: the Jolof page does name Niumi, Baddibu, Nyani and Wuli ("likely responsible for subduing the Mandinka states on the northern bank of the Gambia") - the year (1450s) is Eler's reign, so confidence 1 stays. (d) Njiayeen Sabur and Thieung have no coordinates on any page; both stay at the Linguère proxy and are marked as proxies. (e) Cayor and Baol: the Cayor page, re-read, gives no integration year and describes a tributary Great Lamane; kept as a gain at c1 because the Jolof page says 'absorbed early on' and cayor's founding in 1549 mirrors the loss.
